risks.note: Backfill picked started_at (not run_date) as the month source for real-source rows because run_date was NULL for 9 of the 15 s3 rows at migration time. All resulting ym values land in 2026-11 which matches the actual run month; no cross-month flights were in the backfilled range.

The 77 collapsed rows were all from pre-migration matrix sweeps that reran cells without a constraint. Their eval_results rows were ON DELETE CASCADE'd away automatically. Row count in eval_results dropped correspondingly - any dashboard query that aggregated by run_id will see a one-time drop; queries that aggregate by (source, method, noise, metric) see the same shape (max per group is preserved via 'keep highest run_id').

Architecture section 2.3 asks for UNKNOWN-ym rows to not exist. The backfill CASE includes an UNKNOWN fallback for defensiveness, but 0 rows hit it (no pipeline_runs row has both started_at IS NULL AND run_date IS NULL). If future legacy data is loaded, those rows would get 'UNKNOWN' as ym and need manual repair before the UNIQUE constraint can tolerate them.

contract_deviations_vs_architecture: Architecture section 2.3 shows duplicate-collapse via 'DELETE p1 USING p2 WHERE p1.run_id < p2.run_id AND tuple match'. T-01B uses WITH ranked ROW_NUMBER() window pattern instead. Same set-theoretic result (keep max run_id per group); window pattern is O(n log n) and preferred.

Architecture section 2.3 shows backfill as 'to_char(run_date, YYYY-MM)'. T-01B uses CASE on source to emit SYN-002A sentinel for synthetic (architecture 2.3 footnote names this sentinel), started_at as primary month source for real rows (run_date was NULL for a majority of them at migration time), and UNKNOWN final fallback. Zero rows hit UNKNOWN.
